scope: The spec provenance matrix and the issue-link model, with issue_id an opaque external payload. Belongs here: the matrix rows and their sort and render; the role:ID parse into (req_id, issue_id, role); issue_id is projected only, never a key. Does not belong here: resolving an issue id to a title (TRK); requirement identity or routing. Boundary case: an issue id shaped like KEY-NNN stays an opaque string and is never resolved against the requirements table.

requirements.statement: spec provenance treats every issue_id as an opaque payload — never a PK, FK, UNIQUE, index, or JOIN key — so an issue link can never silently become an identity or routing construct.
requirements.why: If an issue id became a join or routing key, an issue-link collision would silently reroute a requirement's provenance to the wrong requirement — corrupting the audit trail the provenance matrix exists to preserve.

requirements.statement: When resolved issue data is served from an expired cache after a failed refresh, spec provenance shall label it stale in both text and JSON output.
requirements.why: An old tracker title rendered as current is a quiet lie — degraded data must say it is degraded.

requirements.statement: When an authoring command is run with an issue flag, the spec CLI shall record the ticket id as provenance on the entry — created on a new requirement, supersedes-via on a superseded predecessor, amends-via on an amendment — never as identity or routing.
requirements.why: The engine warned about missing supersedes-via provenance while offering no way to write it — provenance the tool demands but cannot record is provenance that never exists.

requirements.statement: The spec CLI shall store and display an issue id verbatim as an opaque string; an issue id shall never be resolved against the requirements table, shall never route provenance between requirements, and colliding issue ids shall coexist without merging.
requirements.why: If an issue id became a join or routing key, an issue-link collision would silently reroute a requirement's provenance to the wrong requirement — corrupting the audit trail the provenance matrix exists to preserve.

requirements.statement: The spec CLI shall store and display an issue id verbatim as an opaque string.
requirements.why: An issue id rewritten on the way in or out no longer matches the tracker, so the provenance matrix stops pointing at the ticket that caused the change.

requirements.statement: The spec engine shall never resolve an issue id against the requirements table or use it as a key that routes or merges provenance between requirements.
requirements.why: If an issue id became a join or routing key, an issue-link collision would silently reroute a requirement's provenance to the wrong requirement — corrupting the audit trail the provenance matrix exists to preserve.

requirements.statement: The spec engine shall treat an issue id as an opaque string, storing and displaying it verbatim.
requirements.why: An issue id rewritten on the way in or out no longer matches the tracker, so the provenance matrix stops pointing at the ticket that caused the change.

requirements.statement: When spec req, supersede, amend, or move runs with --issue, the spec CLI shall record the ticket id on each entry it writes, under the provenance role that matches the command.
requirements.why: The engine warned about missing supersedes-via provenance while offering no way to write it — provenance the tool demands but cannot record is provenance that never exists.
